groups.text: It is currently 19 degrees and cloudy in Berlin-Tempelhof.
With the morning weather set, here is the news.

The massive wealth currently accumulating around artificial intelligence in Silicon Valley may soon face a forced redistribution. Neil Rimer, the co-founder of Index Ventures, believes this shift is inevitable whether it happens voluntarily or involuntarily. Speaking at a tech festival in Athens, the venture capitalist suggested that tech leaders should take a leading role in managing how these riches are shared. This perspective comes from a man deeply familiar with high-stakes returns; his firm has raised roughly 15 billion dollars since its founding. Recent exits, including Figma’s IPO and Google’s purchase of Wiz, reportedly netted Index about 9 billion dollars last year. While Rimer stepped back from day-to-day investing in 2021 to focus on philanthropy and family, his warning highlights a growing tension between the historic profits of AI and the broader economy.

The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine reports that Russia has lost around 1,427,410 troops since the full-scale invasion began on February 24, 2022. This total includes 1,420 casualties suffered over the past day alone. Equipment losses are equally steep, with figures reaching 12,151 tanks and over 414,000 drones. While Ukraine keeps its own losses secret, a January 2026 report from the Center for Strategic and International Studies estimated Ukrainian casualties between 500,000 and 600,000 through December 2025. Away from the front lines, an investigation by Follow the Money finds that FIFA is set to disburse World Cup proceeds to Russian football clubs owned by sanctioned entities. This includes Spartak Moscow, which is owned by Lukoil. Because the second Trump administration sanctioned Lukoil to pressure Moscow into peace talks and limit war funding, these payments risk violating international sanctions.

Russia's influence in the South Atlantic is under scrutiny as São Tomé and Príncipe prepares for presidential elections on July 19, followed by parliamentary votes in late September. The small island nation sits at a strategic crossroads in the Gulf of Guinea, an area critical for oil and gas reserves and maritime trade routes, but one plagued by piracy and organized crime. International attention has intensified since the country signed a military cooperation agreement with Russia in April 2024. Meanwhile, across the continent, South Africa marks Mandela Day on July 18, honoring the former president's vision of unity. However, that legacy is being tested by rising Afrophobia and xenophobic violence. Social workers in townships near Johannesburg report that limited job opportunities have left young people hopeless, fueling frustrations that are frequently directed at foreign nationals who are viewed as competitors for work.

In Germany, Unions parliamentary group leader Jens Spahn is facing accusations of double standards after becoming a father via a surrogate mother in the United States. Critics point out that surrogacy is banned in Germany and argue that Spahn previously spoke vehemently against the practice. Some calls for his resignation have emerged, with critics questioning his moral compass and credibility. Meanwhile, in Pennsylvania, the expansion of artificial intelligence infrastructure is creating sudden wealth for rural landowners. Marilee and David Kiliti sold their struggling 89-acre hog farm for over 22 million dollars to a Blackstone-backed data center developer. They are among 96 families in Salem Township who have split 586 million dollars from similar land deals. In sports, France and England will meet this Saturday in Miami Gardens for the World Cup third-place match. Both coaches, Didier Deschamps and Thomas Tuchel, expressed disappointment that their teams failed to reach Sunday's final.

A new report from Detector Media examines how government figures appeared on television during the second quarter of 2026. The analysis focuses specifically on the period between April 1 and June 30. It tracks the representation of parliamentary factions, individual people's deputies, and representatives from the Office of the President. These officials were featured across various broadcasters, including the Telemarathon and the first channel of Suspilne. This monitoring effort provides a concrete look at who held the microphone during those three months of broadcasting. By documenting these appearances, the study highlights the specific access granted to state actors within the national media landscape.

In the world of sports, a generational clash is taking center stage as nineteen-year-old Lamine Yamal prepares for his first World Cup final. The young prodigy will face football legend Lionel Messi in a high-stakes match between Spain and Argentina. While observers highlight Yamal's exceptional potential, Spanish coach Luis de la Fuente is avoiding direct comparisons, insisting that the teenager must carve out his own path. Shifting to software engineering, PyTorch developers have released a fix for Dynamo to prevent unbounded recursion during compilation. The update replaces certain probes of internal attributes with getattr_static, ensuring that user-defined attributes do not trigger infinite loops when missing names are accessed. This technical change ensures that the compile entry path remains stable even when eager forward functions work fine. These two stories reflect a contrast between the unpredictable nature of athletic stardom and the rigid precision required in open source code.

German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt warns that attacks could occur at any time. He cites an increased volume of intelligence reports suggesting that institutions, individuals, and infrastructure are all possible targets. This heightened security threat contrasts with a violent incident on a train traveling between Offenburg and Karlsruhe. On Friday evening, a Deutsche Bahn railway security guard suffered life-threatening injuries after falling from the moving train. Police and prosecutors say the event began as a verbal dispute during a ticket inspection involving a thirty-six-year-old German passenger. The passenger was reportedly intoxicated and allegedly insulted staff, leading to a physical struggle. Investigators are still working to determine how the train door opened during the confrontation.
After the headlines, back to the weather.
This afternoon will remain cloudy with temperatures between 20 and 25 degrees.
And from the weather, a quick look at the calendar.
On your calendar today: Your personal calendar has an all-day event for the twenty-twenty-six summer holidays in Berlin.
And that's it for your personal morning broadcast.
[mature adult voice, intensely emotional, tender, radiant; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
[very very long pause before speaking; then mature adult voice, most emotional, strong, warm, radiant, deeply encouraging; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
